added: #Identify sources of heat. Ice dams are caused by fluctuations in temperature on various parts of the roof. Such fluctuations occur when electrical wiring, exhaust vents, or uneven insulation cause parts of your roof to heat up, but leave the eaves and gutters cold. So be on the lookout for any heat sources in your attic that might be causing ice dams.<ref>http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131346,00.html</ref>[[Image:Get Ice Dams Off Your Roof Step 1 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Provide equal air flow. You can keep your entire roof at an equal temperature by installing a ridge vent and soffit vents around your roof. These vents help to circulate cold air under the entire roof, eliminating the "hot spots" and "cold spots" that cause ice dams.<ref> http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131346,00.html</ref>[[Image:Get Ice Dams Off Your Roof Step 2 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Add more insulation. The warm air from your attic space might be the cause of your ice dams. If this is the case, you will want to install new or additional insulation to your attic floor to prevent the hot air from heating your rooftop. For more on how to install insulation, click [[Insulate-Walls|here]].<ref>http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131346,00.html</ref>[[Image:Get Ice Dams Off Your Roof Step 3 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Seal and Insulate your ducts. The ducts in your house carry air of varying temperatures all over the place. You want to ensure that warm air is not escaping from these ducts. Try spreading fiber-reinforced mastic on all the joints of your HVAC and exhaust ducts.<ref> http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131346,00.html</ref>[[Image:Get Ice Dams Off Your Roof Step 4 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Check your attic lighting. Old-style lighting fixtures in your attic could be generating ambient heat, increasing the temperature huge temperature differences in different areas of your attic. To fix this problem, you should replace all the old lighting fixtures with “IC” fixtures that can be covered in insulation.<ref> http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131346,00.html</ref>[[Image:Get Ice Dams Off Your Roof Step 5.jpg|center]]

#Use a snow rake. Snow rakes are long-handled aluminum “rakes” designed to remove snow from high places without having to climb all the way up to the roof.  You may not be able to get rid of the ice dam, but, using this rake, you can get rid of the snow that is accumulating behind the ice dam and brush it away to prevent any further water damage.<ref>http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131314,00.html</ref>[[Image:Get Ice Dams Off Your Roof Step 6.jpg|center]]

#Use a fan. A simple way to stop an ice dam in its tracks is to refreeze it. One way to do this is to bring a box fan up to your attic, point it directly at the areas where water is leaking in and turn it on. The increased airflow will push cold air towards the water, causing the water to refreeze. This is not a permanent solution, but will function as a temporary stop-gap measure.<ref> http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131314,00.html</ref>[[Image:Get Ice Dams Off Your Roof Step 7.jpg|center]]

#Use calcium chloride. Fill a woman's stocking with calcium chloride, and lay it in position directly over the ice dam in your gutter. If necessary, use a long handled rake or other tool to help get it in position. Over time, the calcium chloride will clear a channel in the ice dam, allowing the water on your roof to escape.<ref> http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/skill-builder/0,,211604,00.html</ref>[[Image:Get Ice Dams Off Your Roof Step 8.jpg|center]]

added: Ice dams forming on your roof can damage your home, leading to costly repairs. When ice clogs your gutters, there is nowhere for the melted snow to run off the roof. Because of this, it pools up and leaks back into your house, causing damage to the roof and attic. If you have trouble with ice dams growing on your roof, there are some simple solutions that will help you to solve the problem quickly, before the ice dam threatens to collapse your roof.
=== Preventing the Formation of Ice Dams ===

# Identify sources of heat. Ice dams are caused by fluctuations in temperature on various parts of the roof. Such fluctuations occur when electrical wiring, exhaust vents, or uneven insulation cause parts of your roof to heat up, but leave the eaves and gutters cold. So be on the lookout for any heat sources in your attic that might be causing ice dams.<ref>http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131346,00.html</ref>

# Provide equal air flow. You can keep your entire roof at an equal temperature by installing a ridge vent and soffit vents around your roof. These vents help to circulate cold air under the entire roof, eliminating the "hot spots" and "cold spots" that cause ice dams.<ref> http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131346,00.html</ref>

#* Make sure you use soffit and ridge vents that have the same size of opening. It is generally accepted that you will need 1 sq. ft. of opening for every 300 sq. ft. of attic space.<ref> http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131346,00.html</ref>
#* Make sure you use baffles at all the eaves of your roof to ensure proper airflow from the soffit vents.<ref> http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131346,00.html</ref>
#* For instructions on how to install these vents, [[Install-a-Roof-Vent|click here]].

# Add more insulation. The warm air from your attic space might be the cause of your ice dams. If this is the case, you will want to install new or additional insulation to your attic floor to prevent the hot air from heating your rooftop. For more on how to install insulation, click [[Insulate-Walls|here]].<ref>http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131346,00.html</ref>

# Seal and Insulate your ducts. The ducts in your house carry air of varying temperatures all over the place. You want to ensure that warm air is not escaping from these ducts. Try spreading fiber-reinforced mastic on all the joints of your HVAC and exhaust ducts.<ref> http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131346,00.html</ref>
#* You will want to cover the joints thoroughly with R-5 or R-6 foil-faced fiberglass.<ref> http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131346,00.html</ref>

# Check your attic lighting. Old-style lighting fixtures in your attic could be generating ambient heat, increasing the temperature huge temperature differences in different areas of your attic. To fix this problem, you should replace all the old lighting fixtures with “IC” fixtures that can be covered in insulation.<ref> http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131346,00.html</ref>
=== Removing Existing Ice Dams ===

#Use a snow rake. Snow rakes are long-handled aluminum “rakes” designed to remove snow from high places without having to climb all the way up to the roof.  You may not be able to get rid of the ice dam, but, using this rake, you can get rid of the snow that is accumulating behind the ice dam and brush it away to prevent any further water damage.<ref>http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131314,00.html</ref>[[Image:Get Ice Dams Off Your Roof Step 1 Version 2.jpg|center]]
#* Purchase a rake with wheels on it to avoid damaging the shingles on your roof.<ref> http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131314,00.html</ref>

# Use a fan. A simple way to stop an ice dam in its tracks is to refreeze it. One way to do this is to bring a box fan up to your attic, point it directly at the areas where water is leaking in and turn it on. The increased airflow will push cold air towards the water, causing the water to refreeze. This is not a permanent solution, but will function as a temporary stop-gap measure.<ref> http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/article/0,,1131314,00.html</ref>

# Use calcium chloride. Fill a woman's stocking with calcium chloride, and lay it in position directly over the ice dam in your gutter. If necessary, use a long handled rake or other tool to help get it in position. Over time, the calcium chloride will clear a channel in the ice dam, allowing the water on your roof to escape.<ref> http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/skill-builder/0,,211604,00.html</ref>[[Image:Get Ice Dams Off Your Roof Step 2 Version 2.jpg|center]]
#* Never use rock salt for this, as it will do more damage to your roof than it will to the ice.<ref> http://www.thisoldhouse.com/toh/skill-builder/0,,211604,00.html</ref>

#* Alternatively, you can fill paper bags with calcium chloride, and toss them up on to the roof, just above the ice dam. With any luck, the bags, after becoming wet, will rip and spread the calcium chloride into the dam, effectively melting it away.<ref> https://www.frentzandsons.com/content/howto/edgeoffwinter.htm</ref>

#Place heat tape in the gutter itself. Heat tape goes by many different names, but they all perform the same function. They are small strips of material that will prevent ice buildup, allowing the water to flow freely through small channels out of your gutter. You will want to run this material all the way through your gutters to ensure that ice doesn’t form at the end of the gutter. This will allow water to escape through the channels.<ref> http://www.icedamcompany.com/ice-dam-services/heat-cable-installation/</ref> [[Image:Get Ice Dams Off Your Roof Step 4 Version 2.jpg|center]]
#* You can install heat tape yourself, but it is better left to professionals. You really don’t want to be climbing a ladder in the dead of winter.
#* Heat tape costs anywhere from $30 to $60 per running foot, with installation included.<ref> http://www.icedamcompany.com/ice-dam-services/heat-cable-installation/</ref>

*Unless it is completely unavoidable, never try to climb on your roof or scale a ladder in the winter time. Your footing and the ladder’s footing will be questionable at best in snowy or icy conditions.
